items.title: What It Is, Not What It Says: Securing Agentic Browsing Interactions with Web Semantics
items.summary: Intact protects AI web agents by isolating webpage elements via provenance-aware representations and enforcing capability-bound execution with user consent for third-party actions.

items.title: LiveMACE: Process-Aware Evaluation of LLM Agent Capabilities in Evolving Markets
items.summary: LiveMACEBench evaluates persistent LLM agents in live financial markets using decision traces to reveal gaps between outcomes and underlying capabilities.

items.title: Failure Recovery via Belief Updates and World Modeling for Long-Horizon Agents
items.summary: BELIEFWEAVER improves long-horizon agent recovery by combining persistent evidence with prospective reasoning and distilling reasoning into a smaller model.

items.title: SciΠvot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents
items.summary: SciΠvot evaluates LLM agents' scientific judgment using 248 human-corrected cases, revealing that frontier models often prefer flawed plans over expert corrections and perform below human levels.

items.title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
items.summary: GPT-6-Astra achieves high performance across diverse robotic tasks via in-context learning, yet real-world deployment reveals gaps in demonstration cost, execution time, and practical embodied intelligence.

items.title: Scene-Designer: Learning Design Intelligence for Agentic 3D Scene Generation
items.summary: Generating complete, coherent, and usable 3D indoor scenes from natural language requires strong design intelligence: the ability to design high-quality scenes and critique their quality. However, existing approaches either rely on general-purpose models lacking domain-specific design experience or learn from static scenes. In this work, we introduce Scene-Designer, an agentic framework that learns design intelligence through complementary design and critique experiences. We construct two datasets: Scene-OTA-35K, which provides Observation--Thought--Action supervision for learning scene design and efficient error correction, and Scene-OTC-15K, which provides Observation--Thought--Critic supervision for learning scene quality critique across physical validity, functional correctness, and layout coherence. Based on these experiences, we propose Scene-GRPO, a Critic-guided GRPO framework that improves design decisions and reduces unnecessary trial-and-error corrections. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Scene-Designer achieves superior performance in physical validity, functional correctness, and layout coherence, while the learned Scene-Critic significantly outperforms general-purpose models in scene critique. Moreover, test-time Critic guidance further improves scene generation, showing that the Critic can provide useful guidance beyond training. Additional analysis suggests a trend of mutual enhancement between scene design and critique abilities.

items.title: HexaShell: A Thin Harness for Exploring the Limits of VLM Agents as Robot Coding Agents
items.summary: HexaShell is a coding agent that controls a dual-arm robot via vision and self-written tools, achieving state-of-the-art results on RoboDojo but struggling with contact-heavy tasks.

items.title: Dream2Discern: Learning from Hard Latent Variants for Runtime Failure Prediction in Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: Dream2Discern improves runtime auditing of multi-agent systems by implicitly augmenting training data through self-guided hard example generation, boosting accuracy without new trajectory verification.

items.title: From Research Goals to Scientific Closure: Evaluating Agents Through Evidence-Supported Physics Research
items.summary: AI agents evaluated on physics research tasks show strong local scientific results but frequently fail to fully resolve research questions due to incomplete evidence and unresolved applicability limits.

items.title: BizBench: Unveiling Hidden Challenges in Deploying Long-Horizon Agents for Real-World Business
items.summary: BizBench evaluates long-horizon business agents on intermediate execution validity using real-world payment procedures, revealing that frontier models frequently violate constraints despite achieving partial goal success.

items.title: AI-Driven Disaster Response and Displacement Monitoring
items.summary: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) has demonstrated its potential across a wide range of humanitarian tasks, offering scalable and data-driven solutions to some of the world's most pressing challenges. For instance, in addressing climate change, AI-powered models are being used for faster and more accurate global weather forecasting, control and design of renewable energy, and monitoring deforestation. Machine learning algorithms analyze satellite imagery and socioeconomic data to predict poverty and promote sustainable development. AI has also transformed disaster response and conflict monitoring, providing innovative solutions for assessing damage and urgent needs and tracking displacement.

items.title: OfficeTown: Generative Organizations for Evolving Agent Intelligence
items.summary: OfficeTown is a generative simulation framework that creates persistent professional organizations to generate work-grounded training data and evaluation benchmarks for AI agents.

items.title: OpenMobile-2: Building Versatile Mobile Agents with Scalable Environments and App-Native Tools
items.summary: OpenMobile-2 is an open mobile agent trained with diverse simulated apps, large-scale supervised and reinforcement learning data, and hybrid GUI-tool use, achieving strong benchmark results and real-device transfer.

items.title: OS-Helix: Unifying GUI Interaction and Code Execution in Native Computer-Using Agents
items.summary: OS-Helix is an end-to-end trained multimodal agent that integrates GUI actions and code execution via hybrid supervised and reinforcement learning, achieving substantial gains on desktop automation benchmarks.

items.title: FC-SWE: Failure-Conditioned RL for Long-Horizon Software Engineering Agents
items.summary: FC-SWE improves reinforcement learning for software engineering agents by conditioning recovery attempts on failed patch feedback, boosting resolution rates across multiple attempts.

items.title: DuoDiscover: Scaling Autonomous Discovery Beyond the Evaluation Bottleneck
items.summary: Evaluation has been central to advances in AI, and it is equally critical to autonomous discovery. Yet scaling autonomous discovery to real-world engineering challenges faces a fundamental bottleneck: the cost of evaluating progress. In real settings, a single true evaluation, such as a full benchmark or serving trace, can take hours, so a search can afford only a handful of true evaluations. We present DuoDiscover, a search system that jointly discovers what to optimize and how to evaluate progress efficiently, through three mechanisms. First, each worker in a fleet of coding agents co-discovers an optimization target and a fast, tailored proxy evaluator, which we call a yardstick. The agent then hill-climbs the yardstick rather than the true evaluation. Second, since search can exploit gaps between a yardstick and the true objective, fidelity tests continually recheck each yardstick's ranking and invalidate any that drift. Third, the fleet is bottom-up, with no central decomposition of the problem. A lightweight orchestrator spawns and terminates agents, briefs running ones, and seeds new agents with others' confirmed work. DuoDiscover enables autonomous optimization from software to chip architecture. We demonstrate DuoDiscover on two repository-level benchmarks and four GPU and TPU kernel suites covering hundreds of kernels. On SWE-fficiency, it doubles the average speedup of human experts. On SOL-Exec, it ranks first on 121 of 235 kernels and in the top three on 212. On the heavily optimized vLLM and SQLite engines, DuoDiscover achieves 1.92times and 1.38times gains over the base code. On a CPU microarchitecture optimization task with evaluations of up to 28 hours, DuoDiscover surpasses both AlphaEvolve-based ArchAgent v2 and the best human design, with 1.65times ArchAgent v2's gain in 16.7 days versus more than 40 days, advancing the frontier of autonomous chip design.

items.title: DLite: History-free Speculative Decoding for Agentic AI
items.summary: DLite improves speculative decoding for agentic AI by eliminating historical context maintenance and using target hidden states for local predictions, boosting acceptance length and reducing overhead.

items.title: PremiseCheck: Efficient Fact-Checking of Human and AI Peer Reviews
items.summary: PremiseCheck improves peer review verification by decomposing comments into explicit premises checked by decision models, achieving high accuracy with lower cost and latency.

items.title: Skip the Compressor: Coding Agents Fix More Issues When They Pick Whole Files
items.summary: CQ2-CARE improves software issue resolution by selecting exact files to include verbatim within a token budget, outperforming compression and retrieval methods.

items.title: Selection Is Not Learning: Choosing Model Futures
items.summary: EvoHeir improves self-evolving language model loops by separating parameter and experience inheritance and using fresh evaluation to confirm updates, reducing harmful inheritance and boosting reasoning performance.

items.title: Xiaomi-Lens-0 Technical Report
items.summary: Xiaomi-Lens-0 is a 4B multimodal model that predicts masks from internal visual representations to improve fine-grained region reasoning and referring comprehension.

items.title: Learning to Think and Explore in 3D World
items.summary: ACT3D trains vision-language models via reinforcement learning to actively explore 3D environments from single first-person views, improving answer accuracy through adaptive, question-conditioned navigation without direct exploration supervision.

items.title: MorphAct: Robot Policies Morphing with the Worlds They Act In
items.summary: MorphAct dynamically adapts robot policy parameters via coupled low-rank generators to resolve conflicting updates across interaction contexts, improving vision-language-action performance.

items.title: BridgeWAM: Bridging Video and Action Experts via Latent Bridge Queries
items.summary: BridgeWAM decouples video and action experts via latent bridge queries to improve action prediction efficiency and generalization in world action models.

items.title: Embeddings Are Overpriced? A Frozen 16 MB Vocabulary for Small and Ternary Language Models
items.summary: Replacing a learned embedding table with a frozen binary code table reduces model size and parameters while maintaining or improving performance on several benchmarks, and enables faster CPU inference with a ternary body.

items.title: Lexical Reference Frames: Interpreting LM Residual Streams in Native Semantics
items.summary: Lexical reference frames interpret hidden states through a model's own remaining layers, enabling accurate attribution, steering, and early layer exit.

items.title: Can Visual Generation Expand What Unified Multimodal Models Know?
items.summary: Visual image-generation training can expand pretrained multimodal models' knowledge, with alignment techniques improving text-based access to that visually acquired information.

items.title: Belief-Trajectory Energy: Measuring the Path to a Prediction
items.summary: Belief-Trajectory Energy measures how inputs alter layerwise predictions in language models, yielding signals for task difficulty, review detection, and model attribution.

items.title: LEV: Thinking Fast and Deep with Looped Decision Models
items.summary: LEV is a looped decision model that increases reasoning depth by iterating its layers without generating tokens, improving accuracy on hard questions while allowing adaptive computation via a stopper.

items.title: Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part I: Topology, Input Injection, Recurrent-State Design
items.summary: Isolating recurrence design axes reveals that a prelude-recurrent block-coda sandwich architecture improves reasoning and context extraction, with advantages transferring to parameter-efficient Mixture-of-Experts models.

items.title: Execution Before Memory: Diagnosing Memory Failures in Video World Models
items.summary: MIST separates scene setup from change execution to isolate memory failures in video world models, and M3-Agent improves instruction execution to significantly boost benchmark scores.

items.title: Sparse Autoencoders Are a Shared Coordinate System for Symbolic Matching
items.summary: SAE-IDF matches symbolic units across heterogeneous systems using sparse autoencoders and rarity-weighted features, enabling scalable neuro-symbolic reasoning.

items.title: StopWatch: Goal Grounding for Object-goal Navigation
items.summary: Explicit goal grounding fixes the dominant failure in vision-language navigation policies, yielding near-expert success with minimal policy changes.

items.title: Resisting Harmful Instructions through Training-Free Weight Editing
items.summary: A training-free weight-editing method reduces instruction-tuned model compliance with harmful behaviors by applying contrast-based edits to model weights using minimal prompt pairs.

items.title: DAGFormer: Global Topology Prediction for Transformer Cross-Layer Connections
items.summary: DAGFormer improves Transformer efficiency by using a jointly trained topology predictor to plan cross-layer connections globally, reducing perplexity and boosting downstream task performance across model scales.

items.title: ARC-SORT: Adaptive, Robust, Compensated Multi-Object Tracking with Interacting Multiple Models
items.summary: ARC-SORT improves multi-object tracking in sports broadcasts by using adaptive uncertainty-based search regions, corrective identity swaps, and appearance-only re-identification to achieve high accuracy with minimal identity switches.

items.title: MTEdit: Packed Trajectories Beat Rollouts for Multi-Turn Image Editing
items.summary: MTEdit is a large-scale multi-turn image editing dataset using packed trajectory canvas generation to reduce visual drift, enabling improved multi-turn editing models evaluated on MTEdit-Bench.

items.title: Consistent Distribution Matching for Data-Free Diffusion Distillation
items.summary: Consistent Distribution Matching accelerates diffusion and flow models via simulation-free, data-free distillation that unifies generation and score estimation, achieving strong one-step and few-step results.

items.title: RAP: A Dataset for Paper-to-Poster Generation via Declarative Markup from Human-Crafted Exemplars
items.summary: RAP introduces a large-scale dataset and benchmark for generating conference posters from papers as a visual coding task, providing verified paper-poster-markup triplets and both retrieval-based and trained generation methods.

items.title: OPMD: On-Policy Mechanism Distillation Beyond Output Supervision
items.summary: On-Policy Mechanism Distillation improves language model distillation by transferring teacher intermediate computations compatible with the student's architecture, yielding stronger reasoning and internalization.

items.title: Stuck on Shuffle: On Attribute-Object Binding in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: A new benchmark reveals widespread attribute-object binding failures in multimodal retrievers, and fine-tuning on synthetic text improves cross-modal binding without image supervision.

items.title: MOSS-Image Technical Report
items.summary: MOSS-Image is an open diffusion transformer that combines high-fidelity synthesis with intent-aware prompt enhancement to generate text-rich, layout-coherent images, achieving state-of-the-art open-weight results on long-form text and layout benchmarks.

items.title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models
items.summary: ReaDy accelerates autoregressive generation by using hybrid linear attention recurrent states to retrieve position-specific context for speculative drafting, improving speed and acceptance rates.

items.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
items.summary: GeoState introduces a view-independent geometric representation that separates scene dynamics from camera motion for predictive 3D world modeling, enabling consistent multi-view forecasting and cross-dataset generalization.

items.title: Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models
items.summary: PPMem is a video world model that uses compact plane primitives as persistent 3D memory to generate long coherent videos with explicit metric geometry.

items.title: Game2Real-Bench: Do Toy Games Reveal and Transfer to Real-World Visual Reasoning?
items.summary: Visual reasoning is an important capability for vision-language models (VLMs) to understand visual evidence, spatial structure, constraints, and state changes. Existing evaluations mainly rely on real-world data or procedurally generated tasks. Real-world data preserve natural complexity, while procedural games provide controllable generation and verifiable solutions. However, it remains unclear whether abilities measured in toy games correspond to real-world visual reasoning and whether game examples can support transfer. We introduce Game2Real-Bench, a benchmark that studies these connections across four capability groups, including fine-grained perception, spatial reasoning, constraint reasoning, and sequential planning. We construct 1,000 procedurally generated game samples with executable verification and curate 400 real-world samples aligned by shared reasoning requirements rather than visual similarity. We evaluate 25 representative VLMs and observe strong game-to-real consistency, with Pearson and Spearman correlations of 0.935. We further study one-shot game-to-real transfer on four models. Constraint reasoning improves for several models, while fine-grained perception declines with game demonstrations. We also construct Game2Real-Dataset with nearly 24K verified game samples across 18 tasks and 65 QA families. Our benchmark, dataset, and code are available at https://github.com/QingAnLiu/Game2Real-Bench.

items.title: AVC-Reward: Event-Centric Audio-Video Consistency Evaluation
items.summary: An event-centric framework evaluates audio-video consistency across complex multi-event scenes by measuring global harmony, temporal synchronization, and attribute alignment via a trainable reward model.

items.title: Dusting the Phantom: Gaussian Allocation for Fading Dynamic Content
items.summary: Dynamic Gaussian representations are improved by allocating primitives based on predicted spatiotemporal destinations rather than current locations, recovering small fast-moving objects and fine textures.

items.title: Speculative Sampling in Interactive Video Generation
items.summary: Speculative Sampling enables interactive video generation with large bidirectional windows by caching predictions and delivering them incrementally, reducing latency without sacrificing quality.

items.title: DuET: Note-Frame Dual Encoding for Piano Performance-to-Score Transcription
items.summary: DuET is a dual-encoder transformer that jointly performs MIDI-to-score transcription and beat tracking to improve timing and duration accuracy in piano performance transcription.
